Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Ealing Alternative Provision’s (EAP) website.
EAP is a school that works with children and young people who have found themselves unable to access mainstream education, usually as a result of their previous school placement having broken down, whether through ill-health, behaviour issues or other difficulties. The process almost always leaves the pupils feeling less than positive about themselves and their future.
It is our responsibility and our mission to support these pupils to get back on track, either through a return to a mainstream school or by completing their GCSEs with us. We strive to put young people in a strong position to take the next steps in their education journey or work life. We endeavour for all our young people to leave us with a future full of choice ahead of them.
Inclusivity is at the heart of everything we do. We provide equality and equity for all our young people and are dedicated to fostering success and providing exceptional support. EAP’s overriding aim is to be a place of safety, security and belonging.
We pride ourselves on providing a rigorous, robust, bespoke curriculum that enables all our students to excel.
All EAP staff maintain exceptionally high standards and expectations, committed to educating, challenging, and inspiring our young people to achieve their aspirations.
Visits to our provision are welcome.

pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Your Future, Our Focus
Our vision is to deliver a high-quality, bespoke education within a supportive, reflective, and purposeful learning environment. We are committed to consistently meeting the unique needs of our students and their families, ensuring they feel safe, valued, and empowered to grow. Through a therapeutic approach, we aim to inspire better life choices and create clear pathways to a happy, successful future.
Respect - At EAP staff and students show respect for themselves and their community.
Responsibility - At EAP staff and students take responsibility for their own choices and actions. We admit our mistakes, accept the consequences, and learn to grow.
Resilience - At EAP staff and students have high expectations, rise to any challenge, learn from their mistakes and have the courage to admit when we are wrong.
We believe that diversity is the cornerstone of our community. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment that celebrates the unique backgrounds, experiences, perspectives of all our students and staff. We recognise that diversity enriches our learning and strengthens our community, and we strive to foster a culture of respect, empathy, and understanding. We are dedicated to providing a safe and welcoming space where everyone feels valued and supported, where we can all learn from each other. Together, we are building a community that embraces diversity and promotes equity and inclusion.

pageCache.text:
CEIAG (Careers Education Information Advice and Guidance)
At Ealing Alternative Provision (EAP), our intent for careers provision is to guarantee that all of our students are equipped with the knowledge and skills necessary to make informed decisions about their future pathways. We recognise the importance of linking curriculum learning to careers, especially in the core subjects.
Our work experience plays a crucial role in allowing young students to develop essential skills, build contacts, and explore potential career options. At EAP, we recognise the value of work experience and aim to provide meaningful placements for our students. We are actively increasing our partnerships with organisations like Music for Children and other employers to ensure that each student can secure a placement that aligns with their interests and goals. Through these experiences, our students gain valuable insights into different industries and professions, helping them make more informed decisions about their future careers.
In addition we fully comply with the Baker Clause introduced under the Technical and Further Education Act 2017. This clause emphasises the importance of allowing colleges and training provider’s access to every student in Year 8 to 11, enabling them to inform our students about approved technical education qualifications and apprenticeship opportunities. By providing this access, we aim to broaden our students’ horizons and expose them to a variety of vocational pathways beyond traditional academic routes. We firmly believe that by ensuring our students have access to comprehensive information about technical education and apprenticeships, they will be better prepared for their future endeavours, whether it be further education or entering the world of work.

What to expect when your young person joins EAP
Young people are referred to EAP for a number of different reasons. We understand that a change of school can be difficult for both the young person and their family. We aim to make this transition as smooth as possible for everyone involved.
When joining EAP you should expect the following prior to starting our provision:
1) At least one meeting with a member of the Senior Leadership Team and our Assessment Co-ordinator.
2) A thorough assessment period (see refer to the attached booklet) to ensure we fully understand the needs of the young person before they start to make sure they are successful at EAP
3) Further Induction meetings prior to joining our provision.

Help and Support for Parents
Are you struggling to get your child in to school, struggling with issues such as money, housing, mental health, family issues? Maybe you need support to be able to access other services or professionals?
Here at EAP we have a team of support workers who come from a variety of backgrounds. (Alternative Provision Specialist Taskforce - APST). The team works on site at EAP supporting the day to day running of the school as well as providing their own targeted wrap around support to students.
Learn more about the members of the team below:
Jennie Truman – APST & Integrated Youth Service Coordinator
Jennie works for the London Borough of Ealing working with young people who find themselves outside of mainstream school and/or working with the Youth Justice Service.
Based in school 4 days a week
George Charalambous – Pupil & Family Worker
Offers 1:1 parent support & group sessions
Coordinates community foodbank services for families
Cally Lonnen - EAP School Counsellor
Cally is a humanistic psychotherapist providing therapeutic support to students at EAP​
​Based in school 3 days a week.
Emmanuel Henry – APST Post 16 Mentor

Testimonials from Parents and Students
"Ealing Alternative Provision has been a blessing for our 15-year-old daughter who was out of school for almost 14 months. We really thought there was no way forward.
Thanks to EAP our hopes have been restored and after just two weeks our once anxious child is smiling on her way to school.
EAP have given us a new found hope in Education. They believe that every child matters. The teachers are so kind, patient, loving and create a wonderful environment for children to learn in. They teach them to become better, not only academically, but guide and advise them on things that really matter in life.
They do not exclude or make the child feel guilty for past behaviours. They have specially trained teachers and psychologists who have managed to gain our daughter's trust in a matter of days. She feels like she is part of a community where no one will judge her.
We very much forward to seeing further progress in our daughters life as she continues to attend EAP.
Thank you EAP for giving our family a second chance. We are so grateful."
Parent of Year 10 student

Key Stage 3 Curriculum
Key Stage 3 Curriculum at EAP (Ealing Alternative Provision)
At Ealing Alternative Provision (EAP), we offer a dynamic and flexible Key Stage 3 curriculum designed to meet the individual needs of every student. All students attend school on-site for five days a week, ensuring a consistent and supportive learning environment.
Our curriculum is structured across five distinct pathways: Opal, Sapphire, Ruby 1, Ruby 2, and Platinum. These pathways are bespoke and fluid, tailored to each student’s learning needs, interests, and strengths. This flexibility allows us to adapt our approach to ensure every student receives the support and challenge required for their personal academic and social development.
Core Subjects: All students at EAP study the following core subjects:
In addition to these core subjects, we offer a range of additional subjects to further enrich the educational experience of our students, depending on their individual pathway:
Our pathways are designed to be fluid, ensuring that as students progress, they can move between different subjects or pathways to best suit their evolving needs. This bespoke curriculum approach allows us to provide each student with the necessary resources, support, and opportunities to thrive both academically and personally.
At EAP, we are committed to ensuring every student receives a well-rounded, individualised education that prepares them for their future while fostering their personal growth and well-being.
We are also excited to introduce our new "Acorn" Program, an additional layer of support that builds on our existing curriculum. This program allows us to further individualise each student’s learning experience by providing a range of small group or one-to-one activities. The Acorn Program offers tailored interventions in Maths, English, and Science, as well as counseling, mentoring, ELSA (Emotional Literacy Support), and safeguarding/wellbeing check-ins. Students can also benefit from Forest School, Outdoor Learning, and a variety of Social Care Interventions to support their emotional and social development. Additionally, we provide EAL (English as an Additional Language) interventions to ensure all students have the language support they need to thrive. Through the Acorn Program, we aim to provide a holistic approach to each student's education, helping them build confidence, overcome challenges, and reach their full potential.

Key Stage 4 Curriculum
At Ealing Alternative Provision (EAP), our Key Stage 4 curriculum is designed to offer a bespoke, flexible, and diverse learning experience that meets the individual needs and aspirations of every student. In Year 10, we provide six distinct pathways: Opal, Sapphire, Emerald, Ruby, Plat, and Diamond. Each pathway is tailored to offer a blend of academic, vocational, and enrichment activities, allowing students to access a curriculum that best supports their learning and future goals.
The pathways range from students attending five days on-site to two days on-site, ensuring a personalised timetable that reflects each student’s strengths, interests, and needs. All students study English and Maths, with the majority also taking Science. We also offer a range of additional subjects, including PE, Art, Film, Sport, Business Studies, English Literature, PSHE, Careers, and Enrichment.
On average, students will be entered for at least seven GCSE-level qualifications, providing them with a strong academic foundation. For those students who are off-site, we offer our bespoke Alternative Curriculum Program, which includes a variety of vocational courses such as Hair, Beauty and Barbering, Let Me Play (LMP) – a sports-focused course, Mechanics, and Carpentry BUILD. These opportunities help students develop practical skills and qualifications that can enhance their future career prospects.
As with our Key Stage 3 Curriculum, we are also excited to introduce our new "Acorn" Program, an additional layer of support that builds on our existing curriculum. This program allows us to further individualise each student’s learning experience by providing a range of small group or one-to-one activities. The Acorn Program offers tailored interventions in Maths, English, and Science, as well as counselling, mentoring, ELSA (Emotional Literacy Support), and safeguarding/wellbeing check-ins. Students can also benefit from Forest School, Outdoor Learning, and a variety of Social Care Interventions to support their emotional and social development. Additionally, we provide EAL (English as an Additional Language) interventions to ensure all students have the language support they need to thrive. Through the Acorn Program, we aim to provide a holistic approach to each student's education, helping them build confidence, overcome challenges, and reach their full potential.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ealing Alternative Provision - Frequently Asked Questions
pageCache.text:
Frequently Asked Questions
What is EAP?
Ealing Alternative Provision is a supportive high quality fluid educational provision.
It offers bespoke programmes of study which safeguard and support the attainment of children resident in Ealing who are educated outside of the mainstream school system.
Who goes to EAP?
Pupils of generally High School age who, for a variety of reasons, are not able to attend a mainstream school.
Where is EAP located?
EAP is in Ealing, West London. Our address is:
Compton Close, Ealing, London W13 0LR
How can I apply for a place for my Child at EAP?
You don’t apply to EAP like a mainstream school. You will be referred to us by the local authority, and we will make contact with you.
What sort of subjects are studied at EAP?
EAP delivers a wide range of bespoke activities and subjects for students. This includes a number of different courses and options at GCSE level, and the traditional range of KS3 subjects to support student’s transition into KS4. We also work with a number of local colleges and commissioned provisions that we use in order to support students' individual needs. At EAP students will still for the most part complete the same GCSEs as they would in a mainstream school.
What sort of pastoral support is offered to students at EAP?
There is a large, dedicated and experienced pastoral team at EAP. We have onsite counsellors, mentors and careers workers. Additionally, each student has a form tutor that frequently liaises with parents.
Once at EAP, do students stay there until the end of Year 11?
Not necessarily. At KS3 and Year 10, we try (where possible) to reintegrate students back into a mainstream setting. We have a dedicated and experienced team for this who work closely with students, families and schools, in order to place students somewhere that they will have the best opportunities for succeeding.
As stated above, where reintegration is not possible, we aim to ensure that students get a high quality education, including sitting the same GCSE exams as they would do in mainstream schools, so no one gets left behind.
Is there any provision for online/home/web-based learning?
EAP uses Google Classroom which allows students to access high quality, bespoke learning, issued to them by their class teachers who know them well and to target activities based upon their individual needs. It also allows us to deliver lessons remotely as well.
What does Ofsted say about EAP?
Our last Ofsted visit was in February 2025. Ofsted said the following about EAP:
"Pupils are supported by expert staff, who maintain a highly positive atmosphere. This helps pupils to flourish and develop a sense of belonging and trust. Pupils rightly regard the school as a safe space."
Please see the full report on the Ofsted section of this website.
I have a question that is not answered here…
Feel free to contact EAP in the following ways with any questions you might have:
admin@eap.ealing.sch.uk
Frequently Asked Questions

Outreach programmes
AP is an alternative provision that provides full, part-time and temporary education/support to students who are residents of the Borough of Ealing. We work with pupils who are excluded from, or are finding it difficult to fully access their school, for a range of different reasons.
All students at EAP have access to a broad and balanced curriculum and are encouraged to engage with a range of supportive interventions.
In addition to statutory responsibility for secondary aged permanently excluded student, we also offer a variety of programmes to support children and young people who are of secondary school age and finding it difficult in their mainstream setting. These programmes can be accessed via a referral from the young person's home school or a medical professional.
These programmes include:
EAP Connect - Home Tuition programme for young people (of both primary and secondary age) that have a physical medical condition.
EAP Include - Temporary on-site provision for secondary age young people who are under Tier 2 or 3 CAMHS (or equivalent)
EAP Extend - Offers schools in Ealing access to high-quality alternative provision.
Further details on the programmes and how to refer to them can be found in the relevant section.
Outreach programmes

Pupil Premium Universal
All pupils referred to EAP are vulnerable and therefore require educational provision as an alternative to a mainstream setting. They are all considered to have additional needs. If a child reintegrates into High School, EAP recommends that Pupil Premium support is in place.
